title: Fold a network, then count what it costs
brief: Count the straight pieces of a one-input ReLU network, build the sawtooth whose pieces double with every layer, then count the parameters, flops, and stored activations that make depth cheap.
hints: Inside one stretch every unit's reading is slope * x + intercept. A ReLU unit changes behaviour where that line crosses 0, at x = -intercept / slope, and only a root strictly inside the stretch counts.
After splitting, test the sign of each reading at the stretch's midpoint. If it is negative and the layer is ReLU, replace that unit's slope and intercept with 0.
sawtooth_network's middle layers fold the previous tent's combination 2 h1 - 4 h2 into their own weights: W = [[2, -4], [2, -4]] and b = [0, -0.5].
Each layer holds W with shape (out, in) and b with shape (out,). Their sizes are out * in and out.
Per layer, flops are 2 * in * out for the product, out for the bias, and out times the bend cost: relu 1, gelu 9, identity 0.
For stored activations, count the input once, then add the number of outputs of every layer, which is W.shape[0].
